newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dlr modest rise expected to continue-MAS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dlr modest rise expected to continue-MAS.

text.p: The Singapore dollar's modest rate of appreciation may be expected to continue, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its 1996/97 annual report on Tuesday.
It said during 1993-95 exchange rate policy was aimed at containing inflationary pressures arising from rapid economic growth.
But as growth slowed in 1996 domestic cost pressures waned and so a more moderate rate of appreciation of the Singapore dollar was sufficient to achieve a low rate of consumer price inflation.

"As long as the global inflationary environment remains benign and domestic economic growth does not persistently exceed the sustainable rate of about seven percent, this more modest rate of appreciation may be expected to continue," the MAS said in the annual report.

During 1996 the Singapore dollar strengthened against most currencies but was fairly stable against the rising U.S. dollar. It firmed on those currencies put under pressure by the strong dollar, including the yen and the mark, but eased on high-yielding sterling and the Australian dollar.
